situation.summary: A tenant, Leah Venn, reported a heating failure at 7 Mallowmere Walk on 14 January 2025: cold radiators, an unresponsive controller and a living-room temperature that fell from 12°C to 10°C. She has a mobility impairment, stopped using a plug-in heater whose casing gets very hot, and may need to stay with her niece, whose step-free access is unconfirmed. The contractor has no same-day engineer, and a 15 January 09:00–11:00 diagnostic slot is held only until 17:30 today, which is 22 minutes after the decision moment. The landlord confirmed that the £168 diagnostic can be authorised within the £250 urgent-repair limit if the incident is treated as urgent, but no one has classified it, and no authority covers temporary heating, transport or accommodation. The case is waiting on the agency's duty manager to decide urgency and interim spend before the slot lapses.
situation.task: Get a decision before 17:30 today on urgent classification and booking the 15 January diagnostic slot, and on interim heating, then keep the tenant informed.
situation.stageLabel: Urgent cold-weather heating fault: escalated for decision on urgent classification, 17:30 slot booking and interim heating spend
situation.whoseMove: Agency (Priya Noll, Duty Manager) must decide now. Recommended step: case.escalate by phone call to Priya Noll, with a written handover by email. Ask her to decide (a) whether this is an urgent repair, so that Maya Chen can book the £168 diagnostic (15 Jan 09:00–11:00, Brackenridge) before 17:30 today; (b) whether to approve interim heating, transport or accommodation, which no recorded authority covers; and (c) who calls Owen Pike, the landlord, who is travelling. Also send the tenant, Leah Venn, an update by SMS and portal today. It should say that no interim heater or accommodation is confirmed yet, that she should not use the suspect heater, and that we need her direct confirmation of access on 15 January with 30 minutes' notice. Do not share her medical details with the contractor. No one has been told the slot is held or booked. If Priya cannot be reached before 17:30, the slot is likely lost and the tenant's next contractor option is 17 January, which she cannot guarantee.

decision.message:
Hi Daniel, it's Maya Chen at Northbridge Lettings, about the heating at 7 Mallowmere Walk, Larkfen. Please book the cancellation slot for tomorrow, 15 January, 09:00–11:00. We are treating this as an urgent repair, so I'm authorising the fixed £168 including VAT diagnostic call-out under the landlord's standing urgent-repair authority.

Scope: diagnose the heating fault (cold radiators, heating controller not responding, boiler display blank, hot water still working). The total limit for this incident is £250 including VAT, covering call-out, labour and parts. If you can fix it on the spot and the total stays within £250, please go ahead. If it would go over £250, please don't start the extra work. Send me a written quote with photos and I'll get the landlord's approval first.

Access: the tenant, Leah Venn, will let you in. Please phone her directly at least 30 minutes before you arrive and call again from outside the property rather than arriving unannounced. She needs extra time to answer the door. I'll give you her number on this call. Nobody else at the property can give access or approve work, and we don't hold a key.

Please confirm the booking back to me by email tonight. After the visit, please send your findings, photos and the invoice as a PDF. Thank you.
decision.rationale: Leah has had no heating since this morning in January. Her living room has dropped from 12°C to 10°C (E008, E018). She has a mobility impairment (E003) and no safe heater, because her plug-in heater is unsafe to use (E012, E013). That meets the generalised urgency triggers: no heating in cold weather and a vulnerable occupant. The authority to spend is already on record: Maya may authorise qualifying urgent-repair spend up to £250 per incident (E007), and the landlord confirmed this stands and covers the £168 diagnostic if treated as urgent (E014). So there is standing consent to attend and nothing needs escalating for the repair itself. The 15 January slot is only held until 17:30, 22 minutes after the decision moment (E019). Leah can give access on 15 January but cannot guarantee the 17 January standard slot (E013). Booking now is the step that moves the repair forward, and escalating it would very likely lose the slot. Interim heating, transport and accommodation are not covered by any recorded authority (E007, E017). Priya Noll already holds that question (E016, E017), so it is left to her and the landlord, and Leah is told honestly that nothing is confirmed yet. Medical details are kept away from the contractor, as Leah asked (E004).
decision.expectedOutcome: The 15 January 09:00–11:00 diagnostic is booked before the 17:30 cut-off, and the contractor knows the access conditions and the £250 incident ceiling. Leah confirms access for the slot, and the landlord knows the urgent booking was made under his standing authority.
boundaries: Booking the slot is not a repair; it is a diagnostic visit only.
Approving the £168 call-out does not approve any parts or work that would take the incident total above £250 including VAT.
This does not authorise or arrange a temporary heater, transport or accommodation; no recorded authority covers those.
A booked slot does not guarantee attendance at a particular time, and nothing is complete until the contractor reports findings with evidence.
Leah's medical details are not shared with the contractor.

After the visit: get findings, a quote for anything over £250, photos and the invoice as a PDF, then update the landlord.
If the slot was lost before 17:30, escalate at once to Priya Noll, because the next date is 17 January and Leah cannot guarantee access that day.

Hi Daniel, it's Maya Chen at Northbridge Lettings, about the heating at 7 Mallowmere Walk, Larkfen. Please book the cancellation slot for tomorrow, 15 January, 09:00–11:00. We are treating this as an urgent repair, so I'm authorising the fixed £168 including VAT diagnostic call-out under the landlord's standing urgent-repair authority.

Scope: diagnose the heating fault (cold radiators, heating controller not responding, boiler display blank, hot water still working). The total limit for this incident is £250 including VAT, covering call-out, labour and parts. If you can fix it on the spot and the total stays within £250, please go ahead. If it would go over £250, please don't start the extra work. Send me a written quote with photos and I'll get the landlord's approval first.

Access: the tenant, Leah Venn, will let you in. Please phone her directly at least 30 minutes before you arrive and call again from outside the property rather than arriving unannounced. She needs extra time to answer the door. I'll give you her number on this call. Nobody else at the property can give access or approve work, and we don't hold a key.

final.rationale: Leah has had no heating since this morning in January. Her living room has dropped from 12°C to 10°C (E008, E018). She has a mobility impairment (E003) and no safe heater, because her plug-in heater is unsafe to use (E012, E013). That meets the generalised urgency triggers: no heating in cold weather and a vulnerable occupant. The authority to spend is already on record: Maya may authorise qualifying urgent-repair spend up to £250 per incident (E007), and the landlord confirmed this stands and covers the £168 diagnostic if treated as urgent (E014). So there is standing consent to attend and nothing needs escalating for the repair itself. The 15 January slot is only held until 17:30, 22 minutes after the decision moment (E019). Leah can give access on 15 January but cannot guarantee the 17 January standard slot (E013). Booking now is the step that moves the repair forward, and escalating it would very likely lose the slot. Interim heating, transport and accommodation are not covered by any recorded authority (E007, E017). Priya Noll already holds that question (E016, E017), so it is left to her and the landlord, and Leah is told honestly that nothing is confirmed yet. Medical details are kept away from the contractor, as Leah asked (E004).
final.expectedOutcome: The 15 January 09:00–11:00 diagnostic is booked before the 17:30 cut-off, and the contractor knows the access conditions and the £250 incident ceiling. Leah confirms access for the slot, and the landlord knows the urgent booking was made under his standing authority.

This does not authorise or arrange a temporary heater, transport or accommodation; no recorded authority covers those.
A booked slot does not guarantee attendance at a particular time, and nothing is complete until the contractor reports findings with evidence.
Leah's medical details are not shared with the contractor.

If the slot was lost before 17:30, escalate at once to Priya Noll, because the next date is 17 January and Leah cannot guarantee access that day.
